title: Wilhelm cracks the ritual integration over the winter
notes: Wilhelm's winter work at Carrick: the folk system stops being spontaneous-only. He judges the formulaic-ritual step 'really easy — someone just needed to point it out'; the remaining work is formalizing the Artes Liberales / Philosophiae contribution.
source: Session recap 2026-07-25 (Ars Magica transcript), winter-1223 downtime.
body_text:
Wintering at **Carrick** while his research assistants are out gathering material, Wilhelm spends the season on **integration and research** — turning his folk system from a curiosity into something with proper mechanics.
**The breakthrough he's most confident about:** his current system knows only **spontaneous, ritual-style casting** (roll halved). Proper **formulaic** magic would let a caster add **Artes Liberales** and **Philosophiae** to the effort *and* drop the divide-by-two — roughly tripling the effective pool. Over the winter he works out that this ritual integration is, in his own estimate, **"really easy — someone just needed to point it out"**: give a caster the finished formula rather than making them improvise it each time.
**The Artes Liberales angle** is the part still taking his time: the obvious-once-said refinements a folk caster never bothered to name. If a ceremony wants a circle, it helps to know **geometry** enough to draw a true one; if it wants words of power, it helps to know **rhetoric** enough to project the voice. Formalizing how Artes Liberales and Philosophiae feed the working is the winter's real labor.
**Logistics.** His assistants are sent west and south to gather hedge-magic insight, carrying **sacks of grain and silver** as payment for anyone willing to teach the "easy stuff." Wilhelm writes letters — to the loose **wizard-circle** he keeps looped in on the project, to his family, and to **Dietrich** (his brother/scribe, back at his teaching post), whom he promises a **tractatus of the generated folk-magic spells** once it's finished. He intends to set up a **lab on shore** (he is chronically seasick and will not stay aboard ship an hour longer than he must), and has arranged for his research materials to be relocated from home toward wherever the covenant next bases itself. Feeds t019, t009, and the mundane vis-factory pitch (t020).

title: The covenant's Isle-of-Man base revealed: Ránargarðr, Nóatún, and Undrahöll
notes: Rewritten (owner review 2026-08-23) as the Spring 1224 arrival description only. The Winter 1221-22 pitch/authorization split to p087; the Summer 1222 survey folded into 'Establishing a dock and base on the Isle of Man' (marked Incomplete). Aura 3 (Magic) as recorded, source undescribed (U1); lab structure ~40£ is part of the ~100£ total in holdings.json.
body_text:
The base sits at **Laxey** on the Isle of Man's east coast, on a Magic aura (GM: 'R3' — aura 3). It reads as a Norse settlement stepped back in time: longhouses built largely of local **stone** rather than scarce timber (a side-effect of the island's mining), giving it more of an English-country look than the arrivals expect.
A stone slipway hauls ships out for cleaning and repair, and a small shipwright's operation is already running. Fields have been sown with the starting money, the grog families who chose to settle have their farmsteads up, and a small creek feeds the settlement in bracing, salt-laden sea air.
The great hall **Nóatún** ('place of ships') — finished the year before, where the coven means to winter — is itself dwarfed by **Undrahöll** ('Hall of Wonders') rising on the promontory above the harbour: Valdemar's laboratory-hall. One enormous longhouse (~4,500 sq ft), a single structure wider in the belly, with a gallery walk end to end and modern amenities (fireplaces); the working lab-chamber is walled off for Safety, living quarters are reserved for Valdemar and Rán, and the whole faces the sea for the idyllic-surroundings benefit. It is kitted with the best tools and equipment, which drive the cost far past the ~40£ structure toward the ~100£ total. The township is effectively built AROUND the lab — a university town.
A mundane custos/majordomo runs the place (see the following event). The site's recorded history is thin enough that the covenant is effectively its founder — it may or may not have been a harbour before 1220.
The arrivals react in character: Wilhelm — a sophisticated urbanite — is seasick and does not even register the style as Norse; Dustin is awed by the scale and a little jealous of the space beside his cramped shipboard lab; Éogan is excited by what a proper laboratory makes possible (inventing spells).

title: Regiones the Third: the frog-folk ambush (cliffhanger)
notes: s16 reached (cliffhanger). The murfolk (frog-folk) confirmed as the Level-3 colony. Session ended here; next session opens on the ambush.
body_text:
Crossing into Level 3: a bioluminescent marsh — fungi above and below the water, paths that dip between deep pools, and **underwater 'homesteads'** framed in light, with figures moving in the depths.
An arrow lands at Garrett's feet; a dart strikes Dagmar's neck and drops him into a hallucinatory (not unconscious) state. As he goes under he locks eyes with the shooter — not a merman like Ka'wa'ill but a grotesque, intelligent **frog-fish person** (the murfolk).
Ambush sprung; the scene is paused here — next session opens on dealing with it.

title: Valdemar pitches an Isle-of-Man base — and the covenant authorizes it
notes: Split from the former p078 'base revealed' event (owner review 2026-08-23): the Winter 1221-22 pitch + authorization. Leads into the Summer 1222 survey ('Establishing a dock and base on the Isle of Man', now Incomplete) and the Spring 1224 arrival (p078).
body_text:
Wintering in Bruges is expensive and yields little, so over the winter Valdemar proposes the covenant establish an anchorage of its own — a remote place to winter, haul ships up for repair, and house grog families — funded largely by his own piracy rather than the covenant purse.
He argues for seeking the local lord's PERMISSION and legitimate title rather than squatting a pirate's cove ('permission rather than forgiveness'), and asks for ~50 Mythic pounds to start (of a ~130£ full estimate — 5£ quarters per magus, 1£ per grog family, plus construction).
The magi debate: Dagmar is wary of tying resources to a stationary site (the covenant is deliberately mobile) unless it sits on a strong Magic aura they can claim; Éogan is for it if it pays its way; all agree it must generate income, not be a financial sink.
Peripheral-Code note raised: magi may not swear fealty or serve as court wizards, but may hold a landed site; the Isle of Man's jurisdictional grey zone — not clearly in any Tribunal — is a feature Valdemar sought.
The covenant authorizes the venture; Valdemar will scout and establish it.
